findings: src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:333: the change is one line. Before it, a DELIM_GET build side ran IsFiltering on children[0], which is the probe side. That is almost certainly a bug, and it meant DELIM joins rarely got a Bloom filter. Setting the flag to true is a reasonable general heuristic: a DELIM_GET emits the distinct outer keys, so it acts like a filtered build side.

build_side_has_filter is only read in PhysicalHashJoin::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:888), together with can_use_bf and the probe-larger-than-build check. It decides whether a Bloom filter is worth building. It does not affect correctness. Which join types and conditions are eligible for pushdown is still decided upstream, when probe_info is populated, so no new correctness surface is added.

Nothing checks for a particular query, table or literal. The change applies to any decorrelated subquery that uses a DELIM join. When the filter is not selective, it is still switched off at runtime by the selectivity filter.
